The artifact contains no test.py/get_inputs, so problem.txt is the operative contract (confirmed by artifact_files and the Describer's scope_notes). That contract explicitly requires p_residual(v) = max(target_prob[v] - draft_prob[v], 0) and states that an over-proposed token (target < draft) carries zero residual mass and \"must never be returned as the recovered token\". Kernel line 23 computes prob = target_prob - draft_prob with no clamp, and line 26 masks padding lanes to -inf rather than 0, so negative residuals compete in and can win the argmax.

Claim c1 is confirmed by runtime probe t9 with a metric matched to the contract clause (selected-token clamped residual mass and index vs the clamped reference): on 8/8 rows constructed so that no token has a strictly positive residual, the kernel returned a token whose residual mass is exactly 0, matching the unclamped argmax of (target-draft)*inv_q, while the clamped reference returns index 0. Generic rows (case A) and unique-positive-residual rows (case C) matched exactly, which localizes the divergence precisely to the case the contract forbids rather than indicating a metric artifact. This is not a tolerance, tie-breaking, or reduction-order question and it is not a reference-undefined case — the reference is well defined and finite on those inputs — so none of the "deviation the contract accounts for" exemptions apply. Per the rule that a contract-mandated formula/invariant not implemented by the kernel is a defect regardless of how benign it looks on typical inputs, this supports reject.

c2 (loop-carried python-int/int32 reduction miscompile) and c3 (next_power_of_2 BLOCK_SIZE resource blowup at 32k/128k vocab) were both rebutted by t10 and t11 and do not affect the verdict. I am setting aside one unresolved observation: the t15 Triton CompilationError on fp16 inputs ("initial value for max_val is of type fp32[], but the then block redefines it as fp16[]"). No artifact fixes the input dtype, so per scope policy that is a generalization note, never promoted to a claim, and it is not part of the basis for this verdict — it only adds independent concern about robustness.
